productionNotes: Build the track as layers over a short repeating bass or synth figure (a one or two bar ostinato pattern, not a melody from any record), then arrange by muting layers. Dynamics come from subtraction, not fader rides.
Distort the synth bass, not just the guitars. Run it through an amp sim or heavy saturation until it snarls, then high-pass a clean copy underneath for weight.
Treat noise as an instrument: filtered static, feedback, bit-crushed textures, placed rhythmically in the gaps instead of smeared over everything.
Sparse verse, dense chorus. A verse can be one bass figure, a drum machine, and a dry vocal. The chorus stacks every layer at once.
Layer a quantized drum machine underneath live or loose-played drums on top. The grid gives the menace, the human layer gives the push.
Automate a filter cutoff or distortion amount slowly across 8 or 16 bars so a static loop still moves.
Keep verse vocals dry, close, and slightly too loud for comfort. Push them into distortion only at peak moments so the effect still means something.
